questions.text: What is the full 32-bit value returned (as an integer in hex-agnostic decimal)? Is bit 31 equal to 1? (Scenario: After CLEAR the output FIFO is empty and OUT_POP is issued.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: OUT_POP of an empty FIFO returns 0 with bit 31 clear, so the full 32-bit value is 0 (decimal 0) and bit 31 is not 1. Nothing is removed by the read.
questions.evidence: OUT_POP of an empty FIFO returns 0 (bit 31 clear) and removes nothing.

questions.text: What is SAT_COUNT after the RUN completes? (Scenario: After CLEAR, 4 samples are processed where the filter output before saturation would be 40000, -40000, 32767, and -32768 respectively.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: SAT_COUNT is 2. Only the outputs of 40000 and -40000 are clipped. 32767 and -32768 are already inside the 16-bit signed range, so they do not saturate and are not counted.
questions.evidence: Saturation clips to -32768 and +32767 and increments SAT_COUNT once per saturated output; SAT_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps.

questions.text: On how many cycles after h_re at most does h_rdata first show 0x77, and does h_rdata still show 0x77 five cycles later? (Scenario: h_re is asserted for one clk_25 cycle on address 0x008 at cycle 0 with SCRATCH=0x77; no further reads follow.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: h_rdata must show 0x77 within at most 2 clocks after h_re, and it must hold it. With no further reads, it still shows 0x77 five cycles later.
questions.evidence: After `h_re`, `h_rdata` must show the addressed register within 2 clocks and hold it.

questions.text: When RUN finishes, how many samples are in the output FIFO if 1500 total samples are pushed over time in chunks of 1024 and 476 each with RUN per chunk and no pops? (Scenario: Input FIFO holds 1024 samples, output FIFO is empty, and RUN is issued without any OUT_POP; the output FIFO capacity is 1024.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: The spec settles this. After the first RUN (1024 samples), the output FIFO holds 1024 outputs. With no pops, the second RUN has no room, so it processes 0 samples. The 476 samples stay in the input FIFO, and the output FIFO stays at 1024. Nothing is dropped or overwritten, and SAMPLES_DONE counts only the 1024 processed samples.
questions.evidence: If a run would produce more outputs than there is room in the output FIFO, the run processes only as many samples as there is room for and leaves the rest in the input FIFO; SAMPLES_DONE counts what was processed. Nothing is dropped or overwritten.

questions.text: Does STATUS bit 0 ever read 1, and what is SAMPLES_DONE afterward? (Scenario: RUN is issued while the input FIFO is empty.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: STATUS bit 0 (BUSY) never reads 1 in this case: RUN with an empty input FIFO does nothing and BUSY stays 0. Because nothing is processed, SAMPLES_DONE is not incremented and keeps its previous value.
questions.evidence: RUN with an empty input FIFO does nothing and BUSY stays 0.

questions.text: How many samples are processed (SAMPLES_DONE after completion)? (Scenario: CTRL is written with bits 0 (CLEAR) and 1 (RUN) both set to 1 while the input FIFO holds 8 samples.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: 0. CLEAR wins over RUN written in the same clock, so the input FIFO is emptied, the run does not start, and SAMPLES_DONE stays 0 (CLEAR zeroes the counters).
questions.evidence: - RUN while BUSY is ignored. RUN with an empty input FIFO does nothing and BUSY stays 0. CLEAR while BUSY stops the run at once and clears everything; CLEAR wins over RUN written in the same clock.
